payload.vision_scope_stated: Complete. Vision INHERITS se.vision with only the delta stated (state-inheritance): the machine currently asks the agent to vouch for its own work and hands it tools poor enough that the honest path runs outside the lane; i12 inverts both. The to-be world is walked concretely - a session opens, the packet carries every rule that binds it, the agent pages a 132k-char document, searches @v1 by name, searches the RECORD across shipped iterations, makes six edits in one call, and reaches a gate whose mechanical half is already computed. Goal system: four goals with three conflicts named openly and a ruled priority order (G2 over G1 where they truly conflict, G3 before G1, G4 independent). Moore pitch: all five slots filled. Scope: two halves, the lane winning on merit and the machine judging what it can judge, plus the record surviving carelessness. Non-goals: eleven, each one line, each with where it went or why it is refused.
payload.problem_agreed:
KILLER. The delta is real and measured, not felt.

THE MEASUREMENT: 4131 calls in the log. se_file_patch is the most-used product tool at 645 calls - three times the next - AND the most-failing at 28, and it applies exactly one edit per call while se_set_apply batches freely. Six se_help misses across three days ask for reading and searching; every OTHER missed capability in the log's history was built within days, so the demand signal works and this one demand was simply never picked up.

THE CONTRADICTION, which is worse than the friction: the standing porting law requires consulting the design document and v1 on every piece of porting work, and until today the lane could open neither - the document is 132k chars with no chunked read, and v1 was believed to be an external repo. A process that mandates sources its tools cannot open guarantees either a workaround or work from memory. That is not a discipline failure; it is designed in.

THE COST, on one day: three hand-rolled workarounds, three release-gate rounds each recovering a ruling the design document already contained, one wrong conclusion drawn from a search that answered a different question, and three defects that reached the owner's phone rather than a gate.

AND THE HALF THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE TOOLS. Gates currently ask the agent to assert models_adhered, red_observed, designs_realized, adrs_traced, verifiable and breaks_if_removed - every one a statement the agent writes about work the agent just did. i8d self-blessed ten gates on exactly that basis and shipped three defects the owner caught by hand. se.law-responsibility-never-delegates then ruled the response: the involvement slider must reach zero and still work, so the fix is mechanical judgement, never more human review. That makes 'lint what can be linted' the precondition for the autonomy this project exists to reach - not a quality nicety.

WORTH HAVING? The counter-argument is that this is a day spent on tools rather than product. It is answered by the same log: without it every future iteration pays the same tax, and every self-blessed killer keeps resting on the agent's attention. The retro found the sharpest version of the problem - the state-of-the-art check EXISTS, is instructed in guidance, and is collected by no evidence form, so it has never once been performed. Guidance that is not collected is advice. That single sentence justifies the iteration.
payload.prior_art_positioned:
SCANNED, then positioned - the scan is recorded at frame_delta and this is its verdict.

THE FIELD has converged on three layers with sequential escalation: exact (grep/ripgrep), structural (ast-grep over an AST), semantic (hybrid BM25 plus dense vectors). On the read side the pattern is settled too: offset/limit paging, a byte cap that REFUSES and redirects to search rather than silently truncating, and path:line:text results capped at max_results - driven by context management, not ergonomics.

WHERE WE SIT, with each rejection carrying its reason:
- ADOPT ripgrep as the exact layer. There is no case for re-engineering it, and @vscode/ripgrep removes the distribution objection entirely.
- REJECT semantic indexing over product files, on FRESHNESS rather than cost: an index tolerates staleness by design, and our agent reads back what it just wrote. Disqualifying, not expensive.
- DEFER ast-grep with a trigger: one TypeScript codebase, structural queries rare; adopt when exact search stops answering.
- KEEP se_get_search's BM25 over ledger nodes - the semantic layer already exists where it belongs, on prose.
- DIVERGE FROM THE NATIVE TOOLS deliberately: Read/Grep/Glob are better at the working tree and blind to everything else - they cannot see the record, which since i5d holds every shipped iteration's evidence, and they leave no auditable trace, which matters now that the owner is accountable for runs they did not watch.

WHAT THE SCAN COULD NOT POSITION, stated rather than glossed: the second half of this iteration has NO comparable in the scanned field. No agent tool surface we found makes the machine compute the checks the agent would otherwise assert about its own work. Either it is genuinely novel or the field solves it somewhere we did not look - and I would rather record that uncertainty than claim novelty.

v1 IS THE PRIOR ART FOR THAT HALF, and it is prior art we own: its checklist lints models-adhered rather than asserting it, and its contract keeps killers away from the agent by default. We take the lint and reject the adjudication stance, deliberately, because the owner wants the opposite of v1 there.
payload.success_measurable:
Nine needs across two value props, each with a pass line that something will actually check.

AGENT-SIDE: N1 a 132k-char file read in parts and v1's checklist read through the lane, ONE call each, in an iteration where no script does it. N2 a known line located in ONE call with surrounding context - measured against today's four. N3 a packet at a state to which se.law-whitelist-guards applies CARRIES it, resolved, unsearched. N4 six call sites changed in one atomic hash-guarded call, with the log showing one call rather than a script. N5 a term existing ONLY in a closed iteration's evidence is found through the lane without checking out a branch.

OWNER-SIDE: N6 models-adhered, red-observed and the requirement-field checks decided by a LINT, their evidence carrying the lint's verdict rather than my sentence. N7 no lint in the suite has a third outcome. N8 after deleting every iter/* tag locally, a closed iteration's evidence is still reachable from trunk by hash. N9 a computed check is distinguishable from an asserted one WITHOUT reading the prose.

AND THE SIGNALS THAT CANNOT BE SELF-SERVED, which the pressure test forced me to change: workarounds per iteration, re-derivations of rulings that already existed, and owner rounds per gate. I nearly wrote 'number of lints shipped', which proves nothing. These three are measured on the NEXT iteration, not this one - which is the point.

FAILURE CONDITION, stated in the iteration's own terms so it can be quoted back at gate_implementation: if the lint sweep produces prose instead of lints, this iteration failed, however much tooling ships.
payload.risks_logged:
Register open, four new entries, each with kind, owner and a trigger naming a concrete response.

se.raid-a-wrong-lint-becomes-the-new-workaround-pressure (risk, agent) - THE CENTRAL RISK: replacing 'the tools are too weak' with 'the checks are too dumb' is the same failure with better branding and harder to argue with. Ruled response decided NOW so it is not negotiated under pressure, plus a design constraint carried into M4: lints compute FACTS, never judge INTENT.
se.raid-a-lint-that-cannot-decide-parks-an-unattended-run (risk, agent) - ruled: decide or defer, never park.
se.raid-the-guidance-join-buries-the-instruction (risk, agent) - the quiet failure: nothing refuses, the rules are present, the agent skims. Tripwire: MEASURE guidance size per packet.
se.raid-rg-is-a-hard-dependency-with-no-fallback (assumption, OWNER) - the exposure stated plainly: on a platform with no binary, search does not degrade, it ceases. The assumption is the owner's and it is about the user base.

CARRIED FROM i8d, unchanged and either in scope or explicitly routed: se_run's fence hole, the batch-patch gap, the read-surface gap, the missing config lane, required-arg validation, the board's tab-per-start, the hosted page's false 'Blessed', and se.raid-an-iteration-cannot-run-its-own-build - which has now cost real time THREE times in one day and is named in the non-goals as deserving scope soon, but not here.
